extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent attorneys, and applicants preparing or responding with 37 CFR 1.131 affidavits/declarations and amendment papers
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance from the MPEP on using affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 to 'swear back' references, and on related amendment-entry and conduct requirements. Covers when 1.131 is appropriate/inappropriate, required showings (conception, reduction to practice, diligence), form paragraph usage, genus/species issues, and distinctions from 37 CFR 1.132.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of Amendments — Directions for, Defective
rubrics_metrics.description: The directions for the entry of an amendment may be defective (e.g., inaccurate paragraph number and/or page and line designated, or lack of precision where insertion is directed). If the correct place of entry is clear from the context, the amendatory paper will be properly amended in the Technology Center, notation initialed by the examiner will be made on the amendatory paper, and the applicant should be informed of this alteration in the next Office action. The applicant will also be informed of the nonentry of an amendment where defective directions and context leave doubt as to the intent of applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of defective directions include inaccuracies in paragraph number, page and line designations, or lack of precision. Examiner must initial amendments made in TC and notify applicant in the next Office action; if doubt remains, notify applicant of nonentry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of Amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: When a replacement paragraph or section to the specification is to be amended, it should be wholly rewritten and the original insertion canceled, so that no interlineations or deletions shall appear in the clause as finally presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matter canceled by amendment can be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the canceled matter as a new insertion. A claim canceled by amendment (deleted in its entirety) may be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the claim as a new claim with a new claim number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discourtesy of Applicant or Attorney (37 CFR 1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and their attorneys or agents are required to conduct their business with the Patent and Trademark Office with decorum and courtesy. Papers presented in violation will be submitted to the Commissioner and returned by direct order; complaints against examiners or employees must be made in separate correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical support staff should briefly review all papers before entry for discourteous remarks. If discourteous remarks appear in an amendment, either ignore them or submit the paper to the Technology Center Director for possible return. See MPEP § 1003. TC Director will return paper if it violates 37 CFR 1.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of 37 CFR 1.131 Affidavit/Declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: A 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit or declaration may be submitted to establish invention of the subject matter of the rejected claim prior to the effective date of the reference or activity on which the rejection is based, to overcome a prior art rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective date of references (patents, publications) and country restrictions (U.S., NAFTA, WTO-member dates) govern applicability. The affidavit/declaration is intended to antedate references or activities not constituting statutory bars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Showing — Conception/Reduction to Practice and Diligence
rubrics_metrics.description: The showing of facts must be such, in character and weight, as to establish reduction to practice prior to the effective date of the reference, or conception of the invention prior to the effective date coupled with due diligence from prior to said date to a subsequent reduction to practice or to the filing of the application. Original exhibits of drawings or records, or photocopies, must accompany and form part of the affidavit/declaration, or their absence satisfactorily explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit/declaration must provide evidence (exhibits, records) sufficient to establish reduction to practice or conception + diligence; absence of originals must be explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations Where 37 CFR 1.131 Affidavits/Declarations Can Be Used
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples where 1.131 may be used: (A) to antedate a reference or activity that qualifies as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) and not under 102(b) (e.g., prior art date less than 1 year prior to applicant's effective filing date); (B) to antedate a reference that qualifies as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) where the reference has a 102(e) date prior to applicant's effective filing date and shows but does not claim the same patentable invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 715.05 for 'same patentable invention' discussion; see MPEP § 706.02(a) and §§ 2136–2136.03 for what references qualify under 102(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations Where 37 CFR 1.131 Is Inappropriate — Statutory Bars and Other Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A 1.131 affidavit/declaration is not appropriate where: (A) the reference publication date is more than 1 year prior (statutory bar under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)); (B) the reference U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication claims the same patentable invention; (C) the reference is a foreign patent for the same invention to applicant issued prior to the domestic filing date on an application filed more than 12 months prior (35 U.S.C. 102(d)); (D) the effective filing date of applicant's parent application or an international convention proved filing date is prior to the effective date of the reference (affidavit unnecessary); (E) where the reference is a prior U.S. patent to the same entity (double patenting); (F) where the reference is disclosure of a prior U.S. patent to the same party not copending (dedication); (G) where applicant has clearly admitted on the record that subject matter relied on in the reference is prior art; (H) where the subject matter is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(f); (I) where subject matter is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(g); (J) where subject matter corresponds to a lost count in an interference that is prior art under 102(g) or barred by interference estoppel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite to relevant cases (e.g., In re Hellsund, In re Garfinkel, In re Blout, In re Lopresti, In re Bass) and MPEP sections (e.g., § 715.05, § 201.11–201.15, § 2138.01–.02). 1.131 is designed to overcome non-statutory-bar references (102(a), 102(e) in some cases) but not the listed inapplicable categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Date of References — U.S. Patents and Publications
rubrics_metrics.description: When a U.S. patent, U.S. patent application publication, or WIPO publication is used as a reference, its effective date as prior art is determined under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) and related MPEP sections. If the portion relied on was introduced by amendment and constitutes new matter, the date to be overcome is the date of amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The effective date of a domestic patent when used as a reference is not the foreign filing date; where the reference claims benefit of an earlier filed application, effective filing date is determined under 35 U.S.C. 102(e). See MPEP §§ 706.02(a), 2136–2136.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed Publications — Effective Date
rubrics_metrics.description: A printed publication, including a published foreign patent application, is effective as of its publication date, not its date of receipt by the publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For additional information about effective dates of printed publications, see MPEP §§ 2128–2128.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities — Effective Date for Activities Used as References
rubrics_metrics.description: The effective date of an activity used to reject claims is the date the activity was first known to have occurred (e.g., evidence of prior use or knowledge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may make admissions or submit evidence of use or knowledge; examiner may have personal knowledge. See MPEP § 706.02(c) and § 2133.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraphs 7.57–7.64 for Examiner Responses to 37 CFR 1.131 Submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs 7.57–7.64 provide standard examiner language to indicate whether a submitted affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 is effective or ineffective and the grounds for insufficiency. Paragraphs include headings and bracketed placeholders for insertion of specifics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifics: 7.57 (heading 'Ineffective—Heading') must precede most others; 7.58 ('Ineffective, Claiming Same Invention'); 7.59 ('Ineffective, Insufficient Evidence of Reduction to Practice Before Reference Date'); 7.60 ('Ineffective, Reference Is a Statutory Bar'); 7.61 ('Ineffective, Insufficient Evidence of Conception'); 7.62 ('Ineffective, Diligence Lacking'); 7.63 ('Ineffective, Insufficient Evidence of Actual Reduction to Practice'); 7.64 ('Effective To Overcome Reference'). Examiner Notes prescribe bracket insertions and required precedences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.57 — Requirements and Precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.57 ('Affidavit or Declaration Under 37 CFR 1.131: Ineffective—Heading') must be followed by one or more of form paragraphs 7.58–7.63 or by a paragraph setting forth the basis for insufficiency (e.g., failure to establish acts performed in this country, or scope not commensurate with claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When used to respond to a submission, 7.57 should usually precede other specific form paragraphs; bracket fields indicate 'affidavit' or 'declaration' and other specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.58 — Ineffective When Reference Claims Same Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Use when the reference is a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication of a pending or patented application that claims the rejected invention; 37 CFR 1.131 is inappropriate where the reference claims the same patentable invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reference and application are not commonly owned, priority of invention must be established through interference proceedings (see MPEP Chapter 2300). If commonly owned, the patent may be disqualified as prior art by an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.130; 7.58 must be preceded by 7.57 if responding to an affidavit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraphs 7.59–7.63 — Insufficiency Grounds (Reduction to Practice, Conception, Diligence)
rubrics_metrics.description: 7.59: Insufficient evidence of reduction to practice before reference date. 7.61: Insufficient evidence of conception (must be more than a vague idea; proof by demonstrative evidence or complete disclosure to another). 7.62: Evidence insufficient to establish diligence from a date prior to the date of reduction to practice of the reference to a constructive or actual reduction to practice. 7.63: Insufficient evidence of actual reduction to practice in this country or NAFTA/WTO member country after the effective date of the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each paragraph must be preceded by 7.57. Explanations of deficiencies must be provided in bracketed text per Examiner Notes. If multiple deficiencies exist, multiple form paragraphs must be combined in the proper order. See cited cases (e.g., Ex parte Merz) for diligence rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.64 — Effective To Overcome Reference
rubrics_metrics.description: 7.64 indicates the filed affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 is sufficient to overcome the identified reference. Bracketed placeholders require insertion of 'affidavit' or 'declaration', filing date, and name of the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when the examiner determines the submission establishes the requisite conception/reduction/diligence to antedate the reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.131 Versus 37 CFR 1.132 — Distinction of Purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.131 affidavits/declarations are for overcoming a prior art rejection by proving invention prior to the effective date of the reference or activity. 37 CFR 1.132 affidavits/declarations are for proving that the subject matter relied on in the reference or activity was the applicant's own invention (traversing a ground of rejection by showing derivation or common ownership/assignment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits submitted improperly under 1.131 but intended for 1.132 will be considered as though filed under 1.132. For some 103 rejections (based on 102(f), 102(g), or certain 102(e) situations for applications filed on or after Nov. 29, 1999), proving common ownership or common assignment may overcome the rejection. See MPEP § 716.10 and § 718.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference Is a Joint Patent or Published Application to Applicant and Another
rubrics_metrics.description: When subject matter disclosed but not claimed in a patent or application publication filed jointly by the applicant and another is later claimed by the applicant, the joint patent/publication is a valid reference unless overcome by an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 or an unequivocal declaration under 37 CFR 1.132 by the applicant establishing conception/invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A disclaimer by the other patentee/applicant is not required but may be accepted. See In re DeBaun for authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference and Application Have Common Assignee — Common Ownership Not Automatically Controlling
rubrics_metrics.description: Common assignee of the reference and the application does not avoid the need to file an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 unless a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 demonstrates the patentee derived the subject matter from the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, for rejections applied under 35 U.S.C. 102(f)/103 or 102(g)/103, or certain 102(e)/103 rejections for post-November 29, 1999 applications, a showing of common ownership or common obligation to assign at the time the later invention was made may preclude or overcome the rejection. See MPEP § 706.02(l).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference Is Publication of Applicant's Own Invention or Co-authorship/Derivation
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection based on a publication may be overcome by showing it was published by applicant or on applicant's behalf (not subject to country-date limitations applicable to 1.131 for acts in-country). If applicant is a co-author, applicant may overcome the rejection by 1.131 or by a 1.132 declaration establishing the article described applicant's own work. Derivation requires evidence the patentee/author derived knowledge from applicant and that applicant made the invention on which the disclosure is based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An affidavit by applicant that others were merely working under his/her direction can remove the publication as a reference under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) (see In re Katz). For derivation, present evidence of derivation and that applicant made the invention (see In re Mathews, In re Facius).

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities Applied Against the Claims — Overcoming Non-Statutory Activities
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection based on an activity showing claimed invention was used or known prior to filing may be overcome by an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 establishing a date of invention prior to the activity, or alternatively by a 37 CFR 1.132 affidavit showing the activity was performed by the applicant(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicable to non-statutory-bar activities; see MPEP § 706.02(c) and § 2133.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: How Much of the Claimed Invention Must Be Shown (General Rule, Including Generic Claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit/declaration must establish possession of either the whole invention claimed or something falling within the claim (such as a species of a claimed genus), in the sense that the claim as a whole reads on it. For genus claims, showing one species may often antedate the genus claim (subject to exceptions in unpredictable arts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If differences between the claimed invention and the affidavit evidence are so small as to render the claims obvious over the references, the 1.131 affidavit may need only to show no more than the reference shows. However, the affidavit must establish possession of the basic inventive concept, not merely what one reference happens to show. See cited cases: In re Tanczyn, In re Stryker, In re Wakefield, In re Spiller.

rubrics_metrics.name: Swearing Behind One of a Plurality of Combined References
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may overcome a 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection based on a combination of references by showing completion of the invention prior to the effective date of any of the references; applicant need not antedate the reference with the earliest filing date. The 1.131 affidavit must show possession of the whole invention or something within the claim, not merely what one reference shows if that reference lacks the basic inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant can rely on teachings of a secondary reference to show that differences between the affidavit evidence and claimed invention would have been obvious prior to the effective date of the primary reference, but must still demonstrate possession of the claimed invention. See cases discussed in text.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Rule as to Generic Claims and Exceptions for Unpredictable Arts
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference or activity applied against generic claims may (in most cases) be antedated by an affidavit/declaration showing completion of only a single species within the genus prior to the effective date of the reference or activity (assuming no statutory bar or a patent/application publication claiming the same invention). In unpredictable arts, however, special practice is required: the affidavit must show as much as the minimum disclosure required by a patent specification to support a generic claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited authorities: Ex parte Biesecker; In re Fong; In re Defano. See MPEP § 715.03 for practice in unpredictable arts.

rubrics_metrics.name: When Reference Discloses a Species vs. Genus — Effect on Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reference or activity discloses the claimed species, the rejection can be overcome by showing prior completion of the claimed species or by showing another species plus that the claimed species would have been an obvious modification. Conversely, the disclosure of a species in a cited reference is generally sufficient to prevent a later applicant from obtaining a generic claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See In re Spiller for species-to-species/obviousness situations and In re Gosteli and In re Slayter for species preventing genus claims.
